audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer is built on the claim that Yasuo's Wind Wall (W) blocks Zac's Elastic Slingshot (E). It does not. This is the single largest error in my slice.
audit.why: Wind Wall 'destroys all hostile non-turret projectiles that collide with it' — projectiles only. The wiki classifies Elastic Slingshot as a dash/leap with no projectile component (its listed counters are Grounded: Disabled and Knockdown: Interrupted, not Blocked), and states plainly that abilities like Zac's Elastic Slingshot are not projectiles and pass through unimpeded. The current text tells Zac players their only engage tool is neutralised on demand, so they farm and never commit — the exact opposite of how the matchup is actually won, and consistent with Zac in fact winning it 53.63%.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall blocks projectiles; Elastic Slingshot is a leap and flies straight through it. Your engage is the one tool he cannot answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate places claim Zac's Let's Bounce! knock-up sets up Yasuo's Last Breath (R). It cannot.
audit.why: Last Breath requires 'a nearby airborne enemy champion' — enemy relative to Yasuo. Zac's knock-ups land on Yasuo and Yasuo's allies, who are not Yasuo's enemies, so they never make him ult-eligible; the wiki further notes self-applied and allied-applied airborne displacements do not allow Last Breath to target the champion. The current advice ('a greedy engage actively feeds him', 'engage only when his R is down') talks Zac players out of using their ultimate for a reason that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Your knock-ups never enable his Last Breath — he needs his own side to airborne one of your team. Engage without that fear.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Last Breath: blinks to an Airborne enemy champion)

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Zac wins 53.63% but the chart gives Yasuo 7/7 stages vs 0.'
audit.why: A 7/7 sweep was only defensible because of the false Wind Wall premise. With that removed, Yasuo keeps levels 1-2 on Steel Tempest range and the flow shield, and level 6 on his own Q3-into-R threat; Zac takes over from first item as a tank whose engage cannot be denied. 317 games at 53.63% is a solid sample and it should not read as a 7/0 loss.
audit.corrected: win[2] -> Skill, win[3] -> Skill, win[5] -> Zac, win[6] -> Zac (Yasuo 3 / Skill 2 / Zac 2).

audit.whatIsWrong: GENERATOR BUG: throughout the full layer, the ability tracked as Yasuo's is 'Elastic Slingshot' — which is Zac's own E. Yasuo has no such ability.
audit.why: focus.text is 'Yasuo Elastic Slingshot' with letters ['E'], and that value is interpolated into tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, ahead, breakdown.early/mid/cooldowns/spikes/feeding/difficulty, phases[1,3,5].why, dosFull and report — producing lines like 'Yasuo wins by landing Elastic Slingshot' and 'Yasuo: Elastic Slingshot online'. The correct tracked ability is Wind Wall (W), 25/23/21/19/17s for 4s.
audit.corrected: Track Wind Wall (W), 25s at rank 1 for 4 seconds of cover — not Zac's own E.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer gives Sweeping Blade (E) any trading context despite it being his entire spacing tool.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade is a near-zero cooldown dash through a target enemy but 'cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds'. Against a lone Zac with no minions nearby, Yasuo's mobility collapses — he can dash through Zac once and then has nothing. Fighting where the wave is thin is a concrete, kit-derived positioning rule.
audit.corrected: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds, so fight him away from the wave and his mobility dies.

edits.before: Yasuo's Wind Wall (W) eats your Stretching Strikes (Q) and, more importantly, your Elastic Slingshot (E) projectile — if he walls your engage you've wasted your whole trade pattern and he punishes with Steel Tempest (Q) pokes.
edits.after: Wind Wall (W) blocks projectiles, and Elastic Slingshot (E) is a leap — it flies straight through. Your engage is the one tool he cannot wall, so stop holding it: E in, then W the percent-HP ticks while he burns Sweeping Blade.

edits.before: Level 6 doesn't save you: if you E in and he has Last Breath (R) plus a knock-up from his own Q3 or a jungler, he can airborne-chain you, and Wind Wall still denies your ranged engage on demand.
edits.after: Level 6 is not the trap it looks like: Last Breath (R) needs an airborne enemy of HIS, so your own knock-ups never feed it. He has to land his own Q3 tornado first — that is the cue to disengage.

edits.before: In teamfights Yasuo hard-punishes your R: your Let's Bounce! knock-up is exactly the airborne he wants for Last Breath, so a careless engage feeds him a five-man ult setup.
edits.after: In teamfights your R does not feed Last Breath — he cannot ult off a knock-up you put on his own team. Engage freely; his ult needs his side to airborne one of yours first.

edits.before: Yasuo controls the early game because Wind Wall (W) directly counters your kit — it blocks your Stretching Strikes (Q) poke and, critically, your Elastic Slingshot (E) projectile — so your standard tank engage pattern simply doesn't function on his terms, and his Steel Tempest (Q) out-ranges your safe farming.
edits.after: Yasuo bullies the early levels with Steel Tempest (Q) range and his flow shield, but Wind Wall does not counter your kit the way it looks: it destroys projectiles, and Elastic Slingshot is a leap that passes straight through. Farm the first two levels, then stop respecting a wall that cannot stop your engage.

edits.before: Through 3-6 nothing shifts in your favor: he stacks flow shield, his Q3 tornado threatens a knock-up, and if you dash in with E while his Wind Wall is up you've thrown your engage for free, so this is a farm-and-survive lane where you look to roam or wait for your jungler.
edits.after: Through 3-6 the lane turns: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 for four seconds of cover, and it cannot stop your E anyway, so your engage is available every 15-18s against it. Bait his Sweeping Blade dashes off the wave, then E-Q-W him while his flow shield is down.

edits.before: Even at 2+ items Yasuo stays ahead in this specific pairing: your Let's Bounce! knock-up is the ideal airborne setup for his Last Breath (R), so a greedy engage actively feeds him, and Wind Wall keeps denying your ranged initiation — engage only when his W is down and your team can follow the CC.
edits.after: At 2+ items your tank stats and unwallable engage carry: Let's Bounce! cannot be walled and does not set up his Last Breath, because he can only ult an airborne enemy of his own team. Engage when his Sweeping Blade has no minions to dash through and your team can follow the CC.

notes: HIGHEST-PRIORITY ITEM IN THIS SLICE. Two verified, matchup-inverting errors: (1) Wind Wall does NOT block Elastic Slingshot — it destroys projectiles and Zac's E is a leap; (2) Zac's knock-ups can NEVER set up Last Breath, because Yasuo needs an airborne ENEMY of his own side. Both were stated as fact across the content layer and both push Zac players into passive play in a lane they win 53.63% of the time. GENERATOR BUG worth fixing at source: CHAMP_FULL.zac.yasuo.focus is set to {text:'Yasuo Elastic Slingshot', letters:['E']} — Zac's own E attributed to Yasuo. That value is interpolated everywhere, so dosFull[0..2] and report[1,5,9,10,12,13] still contain 'Yasuo Elastic Slingshot' after my edits; I did not propose edits to dosFull/report because their array-of-objects shape has no documented before/after path form. Fixing focus to 'Yasuo Wind Wall' / letters ['W'] and regenerating would clear all of them at once. NOT VERIFIED, left alone: whether Wind Wall blocks Zac's Stretching Strikes (Q) — the old text asserted it did; I removed the E claim only and made no claim about Q either way. Also unverified across this dataset: whether hard CC interrupts Let's Bounce! mid-bounce.
